name: ŠK Slovan Bratislava
content:
ŠK Slovan Bratislava is the most successful football club in Slovakia, founded on 3 May 1919 in Bratislava as I. ČsŠK Bratislava. In its early decades, the club quickly became one of the leading teams in Slovak and later Czechoslovak football, winning regional titles in the 1920s and establishing itself as a consistent top-tier side. Over time, the club underwent several name changes due to political and structural shifts in the country, eventually becoming known as ŠK Slovan Bratislava.

During the Czechoslovak era, Slovan achieved major domestic and international recognition. The club won the Czechoslovak league title and regularly contributed players to the national team. Its greatest achievement came in 1969, when Slovan won the European Cup Winners’ Cup by defeating FC Barcelona 3–2 in the final, becoming the only club from the former Czechoslovakia to win a major UEFA competition. This period is often regarded as the golden era of the club, with several players also part of the Czechoslovakia squad that achieved international success in the 1960s and 1970s.

After the dissolution of Czechoslovakia in 1993, Slovan Bratislava became a dominant force in the newly formed Slovak league, winning multiple national championships in the 1990s. Despite periods of financial difficulty and even relegation in the early 2000s, the club recovered and returned to domestic dominance, regularly winning league titles and cups. In modern times, Slovan has also participated in European competitions, continuing to represent Slovak football on the international stage.

name: MŠK Žilina
content:
MŠK Žilina is a Slovak football club based in the city of Žilina, founded in 1908. It is one of the oldest and most traditional clubs in Slovak football, originally established under the name Zsolnai Testgyakorlók Köre during the Austro-Hungarian period. The club’s colors are yellow and green, and it plays its home matches at Štadión pod Dubňom.

Throughout the Czechoslovak era, Žilina was a regular participant in the national top division, achieving solid results and developing a reputation for producing talented players. One of its early highlights came in the 1960s, when the club reached the national cup final and competed in European competitions such as the Cup Winners’ Cup. Although it did not consistently win major trophies during this period, it remained an important team in the region.

After the independence of Slovakia in 1993, MŠK Žilina became one of the strongest clubs in the national league. The club won multiple Slovak league titles, especially in the 2000s, when it established itself as a dominant force in domestic football. Žilina also participated in UEFA competitions, including the Champions League group stage, and became well known for developing and exporting players to stronger European leagues.

name: FC VSS Košice
content:
FC VSS Košice was a Slovak football club based in Košice with a long and complex history dating back to the early 20th century. The club was originally founded in 1903 as Kassai AC and went through numerous name changes and reorganisations over the decades, reflecting political and structural changes in the region. It became one of the key football institutions in eastern Slovakia and later in Czechoslovakia.

The club experienced its most successful periods during the 1970s and 1990s. In total, it won the Slovak top division twice, the Slovak Cup multiple times, and also achieved success in the Czechoslovak Cup. FC VSS Košice was a regular participant in the highest levels of Czechoslovak and later Slovak football, and it produced several notable players, including members of the 1976 European Championship-winning Czechoslovakia squad such as Dušan Galis and Jaroslav Pollák.

Despite its sporting successes, the club struggled with financial instability in later years. After several restructurings and name changes, it eventually competed under the name FC VSS Košice before being dissolved in 2017 due to financial problems. Following its disappearance, new clubs in Košice emerged, but FC VSS Košice remains remembered as one of the most historically significant football teams in Slovakia.

name: FC Petržalka
content:
FC Petržalka is a Slovak football club based in the Bratislava district of Petržalka, with origins dating back to 1898. The club’s earliest roots are connected to the sports association Pozsonyi Torna Egyesület, founded during the Austro-Hungarian period. Over its long history, the club has undergone numerous name changes and restructurings, reflecting political and organizational shifts in the region, while gradually developing into one of the most recognizable clubs in Slovak football.

The club experienced its most successful era in the early to mid-2000s, particularly when competing under the name Artmedia Bratislava. During this period, Petržalka won the Slovak league title twice and also claimed domestic cup trophies. Its peak came in the 2005–06 season when it qualified for the UEFA Champions League group stage after a remarkable qualifying run, marking one of the biggest achievements in Slovak club football history.

After its golden period, FC Petržalka went through significant decline due to financial difficulties, loss of key players, and instability in ownership. The club was relegated and later restructured, eventually rebuilding itself from lower divisions. In recent years, Petržalka has been working on restoring its status in Slovak football, focusing on youth development and gradual sporting recovery while competing in the lower tiers of the national league system.

name: FK Inter Bratislava
content:
FK Inter Bratislava is a Slovak football club based in Bratislava, founded in 1940 by the Apollo refinery, which later became Slovnaft. In its early years, the club went through several name changes and structural transformations linked to political and industrial developments in Czechoslovakia. Over time, it became one of the strongest and most stable clubs in the country, especially after establishing itself in top-flight football.

During the Czechoslovak era, Inter spent most of its time in the highest division and achieved notable success, including strong league finishes and domestic cup victories. The club produced several players who represented Czechoslovakia at international level, and it remained competitive throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Inter also built a reputation for consistency, often finishing near the top of the league and competing in national cup finals.

After Slovak independence in 1993, FK Inter Bratislava continued its success and reached its peak around the late 1990s and early 2000s. The club won back-to-back Slovak league titles in 2000 and 2001, along with multiple Slovak Cup victories, marking its golden era. However, financial problems in the late 2000s led to the sale of its top-flight license in 2009 and a subsequent restart in the lower divisions, after which the club gradually rebuilt itself and continues to compete in Slovak football today.

name: AS Trenčín
content:
AS Trenčín is a Slovak football club based in the city of Trenčín. The club was founded in 1992 as TJ Ozeta Dukla Trenčín and initially started competing in the lower tiers of the Czechoslovak football system. It was formed through a merger and restructuring of earlier local clubs in the city, and gradually established itself as the main representative of Trenčín in professional football. Over time, the club underwent several name changes before adopting its current identity as AS Trenčín.

In the late 1990s, AS Trenčín rose to the top division of Slovak football and became a regular participant in the national league. The club also competed in European qualification tournaments such as the UEFA Intertoto Cup in the early 2000s. Its biggest breakthrough came in the 2010–11 season when it won the Slovak second division and returned to the top flight, marking the start of a successful modern period.

The club’s greatest achievement came in the 2014–15 season when AS Trenčín won its first Slovak league title, followed by another championship success, establishing itself among the strongest teams in the country. The club is known for its focus on developing young talent and selling players to stronger European leagues. It plays its home matches at Štadión na Sihoti in Trenčín and continues to compete in Slovakia’s top division.

name: FC Spartak Trnava
content:
FC Spartak Trnava is a Slovak football club based in Trnava, founded on 30 May 1923 through the merger of two local teams. Over the decades, the club underwent several name changes and structural transformations, especially during the Czechoslovak era when it was closely tied to industrial sponsorships and political changes. Despite these shifts, it developed into one of the most traditional and well-supported clubs in Slovak football.

The club’s golden era came in the late 1960s and early 1970s under legendary coach Anton Malatinský. During this period, Spartak won multiple Czechoslovak league titles and achieved major European success, including a famous Mitropa Cup victory and a run to the semi-finals of the European Cup, where they narrowly lost to Ajax. This era also produced several key players who represented Czechoslovakia internationally and contributed to the national team’s success.

After the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993, Spartak Trnava continued competing in the Slovak league with varying success. The club experienced a long title drought but remained competitive, reaching cup finals and strong league finishes in the 1990s and 2000s. Its modern resurgence came in the 2017–18 season when Spartak won the Slovak league title for the first time in 45 years and later added domestic cup success and European group stage appearances, restoring its status among the country’s top clubs.

name: MFK Ružomberok
content:
MFK Ružomberok is a Slovak football club based in the city of Ružomberok, with origins dating back to 1906 when the first football club in the city, Concordia, was founded. The club’s early development was influenced by Italian industrial workers and local citizens, but it went through several reorganisations and mergers over the 20th century. These changes eventually led to the modern structure of the club, which adopted the name MFK Ružomberok in 2003.

For many decades, the club competed in lower divisions and gradually climbed through the Slovak football system. A major breakthrough came in the 1990s when it earned promotion to higher national leagues, eventually reaching the top division in 1997. During this period, Ružomberok established itself as a stable top-flight team and began to build a stronger squad capable of competing for domestic honours.

The club’s greatest success came in the 2005–06 season, when it achieved a historic double by winning both the Slovak Super Liga and the Slovak Cup. This success also allowed Ružomberok to compete in UEFA competitions, where it had notable qualifying runs in the Champions League and Europa League. Since then, the club has remained a competitive presence in Slovak football, periodically reaching European qualification spots and maintaining its reputation as a well-organised provincial club.

name: FC DAC 1904
content:
FC DAC 1904 Dunajská Streda is a Slovak football club based in the town of Dunajská Streda. The club traces its origins back to 1904, when it was founded as Dunaszerdahelyi Atlétikai Club during the Austro-Hungarian period. Throughout its history, it has gone through several name changes and reorganisations, reflecting political shifts in the region and the development of football in Slovakia.

During the Czechoslovak era, DAC gradually climbed through the league system and reached the top division in the mid-1980s. The club experienced its strongest period in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when it achieved high league finishes, including top-four placements, and became one of the more competitive teams in the league. It also earned recognition for strong performances in domestic cup competitions and occasional participation in European tournaments.

After the independence of Slovakia in 1993, DAC experienced a more unstable period, with several relegations and financial difficulties affecting its performance. However, the club rebuilt itself over time and returned to the top flight in 2013. Since then, FC DAC 1904 has re-established itself as one of the leading Slovak clubs, regularly competing for top positions in the league and participating in European qualification rounds.

name: FK Senica
content:
FK Senica is a Slovak football club based in the town of Senica, founded in 1921. The club’s early development was shaped by local sporting activity under the name Železná únia Senica, and it gradually evolved through several reorganisations and name changes during the 20th century. Over time, it became one of the established regional clubs in western Slovakia, with a focus on building a competitive senior team and developing local football infrastructure.

The club reached its modern peak after entering Slovakia’s top division in 2009, following structural changes and a merger involving Inter Bratislava’s promotion spot. This marked the beginning of its most successful period, as FK Senica established itself as a stable top-flight side. The team achieved strong league performances, most notably finishing as runners-up in the Slovak Super Liga in the 2010–11 and 2012–13 seasons, and also reached the Slovak Cup final twice during the same era.

FK Senica also gained experience in European competitions, participating in the UEFA Europa League on several occasions in the early 2010s, where it competed in qualifying rounds against stronger continental opponents. However, the club later faced serious financial difficulties, which led to bankruptcy in 2022 and the loss of its professional status. Following this collapse, FK Senica was relegated to lower-tier football, marking a dramatic decline from its earlier top-level position in Slovak football.

name: MŠK Púchov
content:
MŠK Púchov is a Slovak football club based in the town of Púchov, founded in 1920 as Športový klub Púchov. The club developed gradually throughout the 20th century, going through several name changes and reorganisations linked to local industry and political developments. For much of its early history, it competed in regional and lower national divisions, building the foundations of organized football in the city.

After World War II, the club became more established and spent periods in the second and third tiers of Czechoslovak football, particularly under names connected to local industrial sponsors such as Gumárne Púchov. Following Slovak independence in 1993, the club rose through the domestic system and, as ŠK Matador Púchov, reached the top division around 2000. This period marked its peak, as it became a competitive first-league team and earned the right to play in European competitions.

The greatest success in the club’s history came in the early 2000s, when it won the Slovak Cup in the 2002–03 season and qualified for the UEFA Cup. During its European campaign, Púchov faced strong international opponents, including Bordeaux and Barcelona. However, after its main sponsor left in 2006, the club experienced financial difficulties and dropped to lower divisions. It later stabilized and returned to the second tier, where it continues to compete while focusing on rebuilding and youth development.

name: MFK Dukla Banská Bystrica
content:
MFK Dukla Banská Bystrica is a Slovak football club based in Banská Bystrica, with roots that trace back to the earliest football activity in the city in the late 19th and early 20th century. The first organized football club in the city was established in 1900, and since then the club’s identity has evolved through numerous name changes and reorganisations such as Slávia, ŠK, Slovan, Červená hviezda, and Partizán, reflecting different historical and political periods in Slovakia.

The modern history of the club is strongly connected to the establishment of the army-supported Dukla team in 1965, when a military football unit was relocated to Banská Bystrica. Dukla quickly progressed through the leagues and reached the top tier of Czechoslovak football, achieving significant success in the 1980s, including a 4th place finish in the league and participation in European competitions. After the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993, the club became part of the Slovak league system and remained a stable top-flight team for long periods, occasionally competing in European tournaments such as the UEFA Cup and Europa League qualifiers.

One of the club’s notable achievements in the Slovak era was reaching the Slovak Cup final and earning European qualification in the late 1990s, as well as strong league performances in the early 2000s. However, in later years the club faced financial difficulties and a decline in sporting results, eventually dropping to lower divisions. After a restructuring process and merger involving local clubs, the Dukla name and tradition were preserved, and the club continues to operate in Slovak football while maintaining its historical identity.

name: Spartak Myjava
content:
Spartak Myjava is a Slovak football club based in the town of Myjava, founded on 8 August 1920 as Športový klub Myjava. In its early history, the club developed as a local community team and spent most of its existence in regional and lower national leagues. Like many Slovak clubs, it went through several reorganisations and name changes, while gradually building its football structure and infrastructure throughout the 20th century.

After decades outside the top level, the club achieved a major breakthrough in the early 2010s. It earned promotion to the Slovak top division for the first time in its history in 2012, following success in the second league. Despite limited resources and being from a small town, Spartak Myjava quickly adapted to the top flight and became competitive, surprising many observers with strong performances in its debut seasons.

The club also gained attention for its participation in European competition, playing in the UEFA Europa League qualifiers in the 2016–17 season. However, shortly after this period, Spartak Myjava withdrew from the top division due to licensing and organizational issues, which led to a restart in lower tiers of Slovak football. Since then, the club has continued competing in the lower divisions while maintaining its identity and rebuilding its sporting structure.

name: FC Nitra
content:
FC Nitra is a Slovak football club based in the city of Nitra, founded in 1909. It is one of the oldest clubs in Slovakia and has a long history of participation in both regional and national competitions. During the Czechoslovak era, the club frequently moved between the top division and lower leagues, experiencing several promotions and relegations while also achieving notable results such as a runner-up finish in 1962 and strong league performances in the late 1980s.

In the Slovak era after 1993, FC Nitra became known for its “yo-yo” pattern between divisions, repeatedly moving between the top flight and the second tier. The club’s most stable and successful modern period came in the mid-2000s, when it returned to the top division and achieved one of its best league finishes, including a 3rd place result in the 2007–08 season. Nitra also produced and developed several talented players, many of whom went on to play for stronger Slovak and international clubs.

In later years, the club faced increasing financial and sporting difficulties. Despite occasional returns to the top division, Nitra struggled to maintain stability and eventually suffered relegation again. In 2021, after dropping from the top flight, the club failed to obtain a license for the lower professional tier and was further demoted. Since then, FC Nitra has continued at a lower level, working on rebuilding its structure and restoring competitiveness in Slovak football.

name: MŠK Považská Bystrica
content:
MŠK Považská Bystrica is a Slovak football club based in the town of Považská Bystrica, founded in 1920 as ŠK Považská Bystrica. Throughout its long history, the club went through multiple name changes and reorganisations linked to political and industrial developments in the region. In its early decades, it developed as a local team and gradually built its presence in Czechoslovak football, becoming one of the recognizable clubs from the region.

During the Czechoslovak era, the club experienced several important sporting periods and even reached the top tier of national football multiple times. It competed in the Czechoslovak First League on several occasions, with its last appearance in the 1989–90 season. Although it never became a permanent top-flight side, it achieved notable results in second-tier competitions and cup tournaments, including strong league finishes and memorable victories against stronger opponents.

After the early 1990s, the club faced financial instability and structural changes, especially after the loss of major sponsorship. It dropped into lower divisions but later rebuilt itself and continued competing in Slovak football under different organisational setups. Despite fluctuations in performance and league level, MŠK Považská Bystrica has maintained its identity and remains an active club focused on rebuilding and development within the Slovak football system.

name: OAP Bratislava
content:
OAP Bratislava (Oddiel armádnych pretekárov Bratislava) was a Slovak football club based in Bratislava, founded in 1940 as an army sports team during the period of the Slovak State. It was created as part of a military sports system, bringing together conscripted athletes and serving as an official army representative club. The team quickly became one of the strongest sides in Slovak football during World War II.

The club achieved its greatest success in the early 1940s, winning the Slovak top division title in the 1942–43 season. OAP Bratislava was known for its disciplined structure and strong squad, which included several players who also represented the Slovak national team. Under influential coaching methods introduced during this period, the club managed to compete with and defeat established rivals, becoming a dominant force in domestic football.

However, OAP Bratislava had a very short existence. After the decline of the Slovak State and the end of World War II, the club was dissolved in 1944 due to the disbandment of the army system that supported it. Despite its brief history, it remains remembered as one of the strongest wartime football teams in Slovakia, leaving a notable mark by winning a national championship during its short lifespan.

name: FC Lokomotíva Košice
content:
FC Lokomotíva Košice is a Slovak football club based in Košice, founded in 1946 as ŠK Železničiari Košice. The club was originally created by railway workers and quickly became associated with the industrial and working-class identity of the city. Over time, it went through several name changes and reorganisations, but maintained its identity as one of the traditional football institutions in eastern Slovakia.

During the Czechoslovak era, Lokomotíva Košice established itself as one of the stronger provincial clubs. It spent many seasons in the top division and achieved its most successful period in the 1970s and 1980s, when it regularly competed among the national elite. The club won major domestic honours, including Czechoslovak Cup titles, and also achieved a third-place league finish in the top division, marking the peak of its sporting success.

After the breakup of Czechoslovakia, the club continued to compete in Slovak football but gradually declined due to financial and organisational difficulties. It lost its position in the top tier and spent long periods in lower divisions, also facing periods of withdrawal from higher competitions due to sponsorship issues. In recent years, Lokomotíva has been working on rebuilding its structure and identity, including a return to its traditional home stadium in Košice and efforts to stabilize its position in the lower leagues.

name: 1. FC Tatran Prešov
content:
1. FC Tatran Prešov is a Slovak football club based in the city of Prešov, founded on 25 May 1898, making it the oldest football club in Slovakia. The club originated as Eperjesi Torna és Vívó Egyesület and later evolved through various organisational changes and name versions throughout its long history. It is traditionally known as the “Green and Whites” and has played an important role in the development of football in the region.

During the Czechoslovak era, Tatran Prešov was a consistent participant in the top division, spending more than three decades in the highest league. The club’s strongest period came in the 1960s and 1970s, when it was considered a strong “dark horse” of the competition. Its best league results were two second-place finishes in 1965 and 1973, narrowly missing out on the championship title on both occasions. The team also reached the Czechoslovak Cup final twice, in 1966 and 1992, but lost both times.

In the modern era after Slovak independence, Tatran Prešov has experienced a more unstable sporting journey, moving between divisions and facing financial and structural difficulties. Despite this, the club has remained an important part of Slovak football tradition and has continued to compete in national competitions. It also has a long history of participation in European tournaments, including appearances in the UEFA Cup and Cup Winners’ Cup, reflecting its historical status as one of the country’s most traditional clubs.

name: FC Senec
content:
FC Senec was a Slovak football club based in the town of Senec, founded in 1990 under the name Koba Senec. The club developed through several name changes and reorganisations during the 1990s and early 2000s, gradually rising through the Slovak football system. After gaining stability and stronger sponsorship support, it established itself as a competitive side in domestic competitions and reached the Slovak top division in the early 2000s.

The club’s most successful period came in the early 2000s. FC Senec won the Slovak Cup in 2002, which was its greatest achievement, and also secured the Slovak Super Cup in the same year. As a result of this success, the club qualified for European competition, participating in the UEFA Cup in the 2002–03 season. During this era, Senec also achieved its best league performances, including mid-table finishes in the top division and recognition for developing several players who later represented Slovakia internationally.

Despite its sporting peak, FC Senec struggled to maintain long-term stability. After its strong early 2000s period, the club gradually declined and eventually merged with FK DAC 1904 Dunajská Streda in 2008. This merger effectively ended FC Senec’s independent existence in top-level football. However, its legacy remains connected to one of the most successful short periods in Slovak club football history for a smaller regional team.

name: FC ViOn Zlaté Moravce
content:
FC ViOn Zlaté Moravce is a Slovak football club based in the town of Zlaté Moravce, founded in 1995. The club began in lower regional competitions and gradually progressed through the Slovak football pyramid. In 2004, it achieved promotion to the second division, marking an important step in its development as a professional team. Over time, it established itself as a stable competitor in Slovak football under the ownership and support of local businessman Viliam Ondrejka.

The club’s breakthrough came in the 2006–07 season, when FC ViOn won the Slovak Cup while still a second-tier side. This achievement allowed the team to qualify for the UEFA Cup and also helped secure promotion to the top division. In European competition, the club recorded its first wins against FC Alma-Ata before being eliminated by Zenit Saint Petersburg. This period is considered the most successful in the club’s history, as it combined domestic trophy success with its first international appearances.

Since then, FC ViOn Zlaté Moravce has remained a regular participant in Slovakia’s top division, though mostly as a mid- or lower-table team. The club continues to compete in national competitions and occasionally achieves strong cup runs or respectable league finishes. It plays its home matches at ViOn Aréna, a modern stadium in Zlaté Moravce, and maintains its position as a stable presence in Slovak professional football.

name: ŠK Futura Humenné
content:
ŠK Futura Humenné was a Slovak football club based in the town of Humenné, founded in 1903 under its original name Homonnai Athlétikai Club. Throughout its long history, the club underwent numerous name changes and reorganisations, reflecting political and industrial developments in the region. It became one of the traditional clubs in eastern Slovakia, with its identity strongly connected to the local Chemlon chemical industry and later sponsorship structures.

The club’s most successful period came in the 1990s. Under the name FC Chemlon Humenné, it won the Slovak Cup in the 1995–96 season, which marked its greatest domestic achievement. This success allowed the club to participate in European competition, where it competed in the Cup Winners’ Cup and reached the second round after defeating Flamurtari Vlorë before being eliminated by AEK Athens. During this era, Humenné also featured several players who became well-known at national and international level.

In later years, the club struggled with financial instability following the decline of its main industrial sponsor. It underwent several restructurings and name changes, including HFC Humenné and 1. HFC Humenné, before finally becoming ŠK Futura Humenné. Despite attempts to stabilize the club, financial problems continued, and in 2015 the club effectively ceased operations after transferring its playing license and dissolving its professional structure.

name: TTS Trenčín
content:
TTS Trenčín was a Slovak football club based in the city of Trenčín, founded in 1904 as Trencsény Torna Egyesület. In its early decades, the club developed as one of the traditional teams in the region and went through several name changes, most notably becoming Jednota Trenčín during the mid-20th century. It experienced periods in the top tier of Czechoslovak football, especially during World War II and again in the 1960s.

The club’s strongest sporting period came in the 1960s and 1970s. It achieved a runner-up finish in the Czechoslovak First League in the 1962–63 season and also finished third in 1967–68, marking its most successful league results. TTS Trenčín also reached the Czechoslovak Cup final in 1978 and won the competition the same year, which is considered its greatest domestic achievement. The club additionally took part in European competitions, including the Mitropa Cup, where it reached the final in 1966.

In its later history, TTS Trenčín struggled to maintain top-flight status. After several relegations and brief returns to higher divisions, the club eventually declined in the 1980s and early 1990s. In the final Czechoslovak season (1992–93), it competed in the lower tiers and was later merged in 1993 with TJ Ozeta Dukla Trenčín, leading to the formation of a new club structure that continued football in the city under a different identity.

name: MFK Skalica
content:
MFK Skalica is a Slovak football club based in the town of Skalica, founded in 1920 as ŠK Skalica. In its early decades, the club developed gradually through regional competitions and went through several name changes reflecting political and industrial shifts, including Sokol Tekla Skalica, Tatran Skalica, and TJ ZVL Skalica. For most of the Czechoslovak era, it remained outside the top national level, competing mainly in lower divisions and building its local football structure.

A major turning point in the club’s modern history came after 2010, when Skalica began climbing through the Slovak league system. The team achieved promotion to the second division and, in the 2014–15 season, secured a historic promotion to the Slovak top flight for the first time in its history. In its debut season in the top division (2015–16), the club struggled and was relegated after finishing near the bottom of the table, but the promotion itself marked a significant milestone for the club.

In the following years, MFK Skalica remained a competitive second-tier side and continued to push for a return to the top division. The club also achieved one of its best cup runs in the 2016–17 season, reaching the final of the Slovak Cup, where it lost to Slovan Bratislava. Skalica later returned to the top flight again in the 2022–23 season after replacing another club that lost its license, and has since worked on stabilizing its position in the Slovak top division.

name: FC Steel Trans Ličartovce
content:
FC Steel Trans Ličartovce was a Slovak football club based in the village of Ličartovce in eastern Slovakia. The club was founded in 1938 and spent much of its early history in lower regional competitions before gradually rising through the Slovak football system. Its development accelerated in the 1990s after major investment and sponsorship, which allowed the team to climb from amateur levels into professional leagues and eventually establish itself as one of the strongest lower-division sides in the country.

In the early 2000s, Steel Trans Ličartovce became one of the most competitive clubs outside Slovakia’s top division. The team consistently finished near the top of the second league, finishing as runners-up several times and regularly challenging for promotion. Its greatest sporting achievement came in the 2003–04 Slovak Cup, when the club reached the final, defeating several top-flight teams along the way before losing to FC Artmedia Petržalka in the final match.

Despite its success, the club’s independent existence ended after a major structural change in Slovak football. In 2004, it merged with the struggling FC Košice system, and in 2005 it was effectively relocated and transformed into MFK Košice. This marked the end of Steel Trans Ličartovce as a standalone club, although its legacy continued through the restructured Košice team, which went on to compete in the Slovak top division.

name: FC Košice
content:
FC Košice is a Slovak football club based in the city of Košice, officially founded in 2018 after the merger of FK Košice-Barca and another local football structure. Although legally considered a new club, FC Košice presents itself as the spiritual successor to the historic football tradition of the city, especially that of FC VSS Košice and earlier clubs dating back to Kassai AC in 1903. The club adopted the traditional yellow and blue colours associated with football in Košice and quickly became the main representative of the city in Slovak football.

Following its foundation, FC Košice rapidly progressed through the Slovak league system with ambitions to restore top-level football in eastern Slovakia. The club achieved promotion to the Slovak First League and began playing home matches at the modern Košická futbalová aréna. It also established partnerships with international clubs and invested in infrastructure, youth development, and professional organisation in an effort to rebuild football prestige in Košice.

Although the current FC Košice is officially separate from the former FC VSS Košice, the connection between the clubs remains strong in terms of supporters, identity, and tradition. The city of Košice has a long football history that includes domestic trophies, European competition appearances, and participation in the UEFA Champions League group stage by previous club structures. Modern FC Košice continues this legacy while trying to establish itself as a stable top-flight club in contemporary Slovak football.
